market_holds: Spot $16.62 (sealed baseline, intraday 18:11 UTC 2026-11-10); +4.3% over 5 days, -6.2% over 20 days, 13% below the 52-week high. The usual move is a median 5.8% over 7 prints, max 17.6% (the July print). The front-expiry ATM IV is 115.8% at 10 days, which implies a double-digit event move, but the ATM spread is 111% of mid, so it is unusable. Consensus as of the 2026-11-03 Earnings Whispers preview: revenue $340.3M, which equals the guide midpoint ($325-355M, including about $24M from the 53rd week), EPS $0.03, whisper $0.01, and sentiment 'modestly bearish'. The July guide already holds the memory hit: a $35M year-over-year gross-profit headwind in Q4 (about 1,000bp), Q4 GAAP gross margin 39-41%, adjusted EBITDA -$11M to +$18M, and for FY27 a gross margin framework at the low end of the Q4 range (about 40% non-GAAP), weaker in H1, with opex held flat. That framework was given seven quarters' worth of memory pain early, and the stock fell 17.6% on it, so the FY27 margin reset is shown in the price, not merely known. A secondary aggregator puts Q1 FY27 revenue consensus near $581.5M (+6.6% y/y, column inferred) and FY27 at about $1.62B from four analysts; neither source is dated. Short interest is 12.54M shares at the 10/15 settlement (6.6 days to cover), down from 14.46M at 9/30 and in the upper-middle of its 7.8-14.5M range over 2026 (Nasdaq API). Coliseum Capital holds 15.3% with a board seat (13D 2026-08-03), which shrinks the float. The line the stock trades on is the forward guide (Q1 FY27 holiday revenue, gross margin and EBITDA) and the FY27 framework, not the Q4 headline. The last two prints beat on revenue and still fell on the guide (-5.8% in May, -17.6% in July).
view: There is no visible mispricing. Q4 revenue will probably land at or above the midpoint: Sonos came in near the top of its range in Q2 and near the high end in Q3, and Q4 holds channel fill for the AMP Multi and for the Beam Ultra and Ace Ultra (pre-orders from 1 Sep, on sale 29 Sep, inside a quarter ending 3 Oct). But the Q4 headline is not the line. The reaction turns on the Q1 FY27 holiday guide and on whether the July FY27 framework (gross margin about 40%, flat opex) holds. On memory, the data since July points both ways and mostly to 'as expected'. TrendForce's Q4 conventional DRAM contract forecast is +10-15% q/q, slower than Q3's +13-18%. Its 30 Oct datasheet says consumer DRAM gains have narrowed to flat or slightly up. Against that, NAND is +15-20%, DDR4 supply is tightening, and on 2 Nov Apple called the memory surge 'unprecedented' with further increases in the December quarter. Sonos still had not taken material price increases on existing products as of July, so a pricing action could come on the call, but nothing public shows one. The new products are well reviewed (Engadget 9/10 and 8.7/10; Beam Ultra at $699 against Beam's $499 helps mix), and nothing shows an app relapse. No layoff, WARN notice or strategic action has surfaced since July. The known pieces add up to a print that could go either way by a normal-to-large amount. The two prior guide-driven sell-offs argue for caution on the forward line, while the low whisper, the elevated short interest and the bearish sentiment lower the bar. I cannot show the price missing anything in either direction.

recommendation.reason: The decisive line is the Q1 FY27 guide and the FY27 margin framework. The July guide and the 17.6% sell-off already priced the memory reset, and memory data since July shows deceleration for consumer DRAM against further NAND and DDR4 pressure, which nets to roughly what management framed. Revenue upside from launches and the track record of beating the guide is likely, but this stock has twice ignored revenue beats in favour of the guide. Nothing dated and public shows that the guide will diverge from what the price holds.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q1 FY27 gross-margin guide clearly below the high 30s, or an explicit cut to the FY27 'about 40%' framework, would make it a short. Announced price increases, or a framework held with flat opex and holiday revenue guided above about $580M, would make it a long.

self_critique: The best case for down: the last two prints sold off on a conservative guide despite beats. The holiday quarter carries the largest dollar memory exposure, Apple flagged further December-quarter increases, and a departing CFO has little reason not to guide low, so a Q1 EBITDA guide well below the Street could repeat July. The best case for up: the bar is low (whisper below consensus, bearish sentiment, 12.5M shares short), consumer DRAM gains have faded to flat, and well-reviewed launches with a higher ASP could support a holiday guide above about $580M. Both are plausible and neither is supported by dated evidence the price lacks, so 50 stands. One caveat on completeness: several third-party pages refused the fetch (403, 503 and one site's 429), but none of these were budget refusals of my own tools, and the content was covered elsewhere.
approach_notes: P4 ('priced in is a claim to prove') helped: the July 17.6% reaction to an explicitly stated FY27 margin framework is the proof that the memory reset is in the price. The P3 source list was broad, but for a consumer-hardware name with no sell-through data in public reach, the stakeholder and physical routes came back empty quickly. P8 (stop early once shown) applied.
